controls.title: Control: ism-1997
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee defines clear roles and responsibilities for cyber security both within the board of directors or executive committee and broadly within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1998
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee ensures that cyber security is integrated throughout all business functions within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1999
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee ensures the cyber security strategy for their organisation is aligned with the overarching strategic direction and business strategy for their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-2000
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee seeks regular briefings or reporting on the cyber security posture of their organisation, as well as the threat environment in which they operate, from internal and external subject matter experts.

controls.title: Control: ism-2001
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee champions a positive cyber security culture within their organisation, including through leading by example.

controls.title: Control: ism-2002
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee maintains a sufficient level of cyber security literacy to fulfil both their fiduciary duties and any legislative or regulatory obligations.

controls.title: Control: ism-2003
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee maintains awareness of key cyber security recruitment activities, retention rates for cyber security personnel, and cyber security skills and experience gaps within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-2004
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee supports the development of cyber security skills and experience for all personnel via internal and external cyber security awareness raising and training opportunities.

controls.title: Control: ism-2005
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee understands the business criticality of their organisation’s systems, including at least a basic understanding of what systems exist, their value, where they reside, who has access, who might seek access, how they are protected, and how that protection is verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-2006
controls.description: The board of directors or executive committee plans for major cyber security incidents, including by participating in exercises, and understands their duties in relation to such cyber security incidents.

controls.title: Control: ism-0714
controls.description: A CISO is appointed to provide cyber security leadership and guidance for their organisation (covering IT and OT).

controls.title: Control: ism-1478
controls.description: The CISO oversees their organisation’s cyber security program and ensures their organisation’s compliance with cyber security policy, standards, regulations and legislation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1617
controls.description: The CISO regularly reviews and updates their organisation’s cyber security program to ensure its relevance in addressing cyber threats and harnessing business and cyber security opportunities.

controls.title: Control: ism-1966
controls.description: The CISO develops, implements, maintains and regularly verifies a register of systems used by their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0724
controls.description: The CISO implements cyber security measurement metrics and key performance indicators for their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0725
controls.description: The CISO coordinates cyber security and business alignment through a cyber security steering committee or advisory board, comprising key cyber security and business executives, which meets formally and regularly.

controls.title: Control: ism-0726
controls.description: The CISO coordinates security risk management activities between cyber security and business teams.

controls.title: Control: ism-0718
controls.description: The CISO regularly reports directly to their organisation’s board of directors or executive committee on cyber security matters.

controls.title: Control: ism-1918
controls.description: The CISO regularly reports directly to their organisation’s audit, risk and compliance committee (or equivalent) on cyber security matters.

controls.title: Control: ism-0733
controls.description: The CISO is fully aware of all cyber security incidents within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1618
controls.description: The CISO oversees their organisation’s response to cyber security incidents.

controls.title: Control: ism-0734
controls.description: The CISO contributes to the development, implementation and maintenance of business continuity and disaster recovery plans for their organisation to ensure that business-critical services are supported appropriately in the event of a disaster.

controls.title: Control: ism-0720
controls.description: The CISO oversees the development, implementation and maintenance of a cyber security communications strategy to assist in communicating the cyber security vision and strategy for their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0731
controls.description: The CISO oversees cyber supply chain risk management activities for their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0732
controls.description: The CISO receives and manages a dedicated cyber security budget for their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0717
controls.description: The CISO oversees the management of cyber security personnel within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-2020
controls.description: The CISO ensures sufficient cyber security personnel, with the right skills and experience, are acquired to support cyber security activities within their organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0735
controls.description: The CISO oversees the development, implementation and maintenance of their organisation’s cyber security awareness training program.

controls.title: Control: ism-1071
controls.description: Each system has a designated system owner.

controls.title: Control: ism-1525
controls.description: System owners register each system with its authorising officer.

controls.title: Control: ism-1633
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, determine the system boundary, business criticality, and security and resilience objectives for each system based on an assessment of the impact if it were to be compromised or attacked.

controls.title: Control: ism-1203
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, conduct a threat and risk assessment for each system.

controls.title: Control: ism-1634
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, select security controls for each system and tailor them to achieve desired security and resilience objectives.

controls.title: Control: ism-0009
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, identify any supplementary security controls required based upon the unique nature of each system, its operating environment and the organisation’s risk tolerances.

controls.title: Control: ism-1635
controls.description: System owners implement security controls for each system and its operating environment.

controls.title: Control: ism-1636
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, ensure security controls for each non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET system and its operating environment undergo a security control assessment by their organisation’s own assessors or Infosec Registered Assessor Program (IRAP) assessors to determine if they have been implemented correctly and are operating as intended.

controls.title: Control: ism-1967
controls.description: System owners, in consultation with each system’s authorising officer, ensure security controls for each TOP SECRET system and its operating environment, including each sensitive compartmented information system and its operating environment, undergo a security control assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates) to determine if they have been implemented correctly and are operating as intended.

controls.title: Control: ism-0027
controls.description: System owners obtain an authorisation to operate for each non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET system from its authorising officer.

controls.title: Control: ism-1968
controls.description: System owners obtain an authorisation to operate for each TOP SECRET system, including for each sensitive compartmented information system, from Director-General ASD (or their delegate).

controls.title: Control: ism-1526
controls.description: System owners continuously monitor the security of each system, and manage associated cyber threats, security risks and security controls.

controls.title: Control: ism-2021
controls.description: System owners implement and maintain data minimisation practices for each of their systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-1587
controls.description: System owners report the security status of each system to its authorising officer at least annually.

controls.title: Control: ism-0576
controls.description: A cyber security incident management policy, and associated cyber security incident response plan, is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1784
controls.description: The cyber security incident management policy, including the associated cyber security incident response plan, is exercised at least annually.

controls.title: Control: ism-0125
controls.description: A cyber security incident register is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1803
controls.description:
A cyber security incident register contains the following for each cyber security incident:

- the date the cyber security incident occurred
- the date the cyber security incident was discovered
- a description of the cyber security incident
- any actions taken in response to the cyber security incident
- to whom the cyber security incident was reported.

controls.title: Control: ism-1625
controls.description: An insider threat mitigation program is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1626
controls.description: Legal advice is sought regarding the development and implementation of an insider threat mitigation program.

controls.title: Control: ism-0123
controls.description: Cyber security incidents are reported to the chief information security officer, or one of their delegates, as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered.

controls.title: Control: ism-0140
controls.description: Cyber security incidents are reported to ASD as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered.

controls.title: Control: ism-1880
controls.description: Cyber security incidents that involve customer data are reported to customers and the public in a timely manner after they occur or are discovered.

controls.title: Control: ism-1881
controls.description: Cyber security incidents that do not involve customer data are reported to customers and the public in a timely manner after they occur or are discovered.

controls.title: Control: ism-1819
controls.description: Following the identification of a cyber security incident, the cyber security incident response plan is enacted.

controls.title: Control: ism-0133
controls.description: When a data spill occurs, data owners are advised and access to the data is restricted.

controls.title: Control: ism-0917
controls.description:
When malicious code is detected, the following steps are taken to handle the infection:

- the infected systems are isolated
- all previously connected media used in the period leading up to the infection are scanned for signs of infection and isolated if necessary
- antivirus applications are used to remove the infection from infected systems and media
- if the infection cannot be reliably removed, systems are restored from a known good backup or rebuilt.

controls.title: Control: ism-1969
controls.description: Malicious code, when stored or communicated, is treated beforehand to prevent accidental execution.

controls.title: Control: ism-1970
controls.description: Malicious code processing for cyber security incident response or research purposes is conducted in a dedicated analysis environment segregated from other systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-0137
controls.description: Legal advice is sought before allowing intrusion activity to continue on a system for the purpose of collecting further data or evidence.

controls.title: Control: ism-1609
controls.description: System owners are consulted before allowing intrusion activity to continue on a system for the purpose of collecting further data or evidence.

controls.title: Control: ism-1731
controls.description: Planning and coordination of intrusion remediation activities are conducted using trusted systems separate from a compromised system.

controls.title: Control: ism-1732
controls.description: Intrusion remediation activities are coordinated and sequenced to minimise opportunities for re-compromise of a system while balancing operational risk and business continuity requirements.

controls.title: Control: ism-1213
controls.description: Following intrusion remediation activities, enhanced monitoring is conducted until there is sufficient evidence-based confidence that malicious actors have been eradicated from a system and have not re-established access.

controls.title: Control: ism-0138
controls.description:
The integrity of evidence gathered during an investigation is maintained by investigators:

- recording all their actions
- maintaining a proper chain of custody
- following all instructions provided by relevant law enforcement agencies.

controls.title: Control: ism-1631
controls.description: Suppliers of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services associated with systems are identified.

controls.title: Control: ism-1452
controls.description: A supply chain risk assessment is performed for suppliers of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services to assess the impact to a system’s security risk profile.

controls.title: Control: ism-1567
controls.description: Suppliers identified as high risk by a cyber supply chain risk assessment are not used.

controls.title: Control: ism-1568
controls.description: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have demonstrated a commitment to the security of their products and services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1882
controls.description: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have demonstrated a commitment to transparency for their products and services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1632
controls.description: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are procured from suppliers that have a strong track record of maintaining the security of their own systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-1569
controls.description: A shared responsibility model is created, documented and shared between suppliers and their customers to articulate the security responsibilities of each party.

controls.title: Control: ism-1785
controls.description: A supplier relationship management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1786
controls.description: An approved supplier list is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1787
controls.description: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are sourced from approved suppliers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1788
controls.description: Multiple potential suppliers are identified for sourcing critical operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1789
controls.description: Sufficient spares of critical IT equipment and OT equipment are sourced and kept in reserve.

controls.title: Control: ism-1790
controls.description: Operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are delivered in a manner that maintains their integrity.

controls.title: Control: ism-1791
controls.description: The integrity of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are assessed as part of acceptance of products and services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1792
controls.description: The authenticity of operating systems, applications, IT equipment, OT equipment and services are assessed as part of acceptance of products and services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1736
controls.description: A managed service register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-1737
controls.description:
A managed service register contains the following for each managed service:

- managed service provider’s name
- managed service’s name
- purpose for using the managed service
- sensitivity or classification of data involved
- due date for the next security control assessment of the managed service
- contractual arrangements for the managed service
- organisational point of contact for the managed service
- 24/7 contact details for the managed service provider.

controls.title: Control: ism-1793
controls.description: Managed service providers and their non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET managed services undergo an Infosec Registered Assessor Program (IRAP) assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

controls.title: Control: ism-1971
controls.description: Managed service providers and their TOP SECRET managed services, including sensitive compartmented information managed services, undergo a security control assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the security control assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

controls.title: Control: ism-1637
controls.description: An outsourced cloud service register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-1638
controls.description:
An outsourced cloud service register contains the following for each outsourced cloud service:

- cloud service provider’s name
- cloud service’s name
- purpose for using the cloud service
- sensitivity or classification of data involved
- due date for the next security control assessment of the cloud service
- contractual arrangements for the cloud service
- organisational point of contact for the cloud service
- 24/7 contact details for the cloud service provider.

controls.title: Control: ism-1529
controls.description: Only community or private clouds are used for outsourced SECRET and TOP SECRET cloud services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1570
controls.description: Outsourced cloud service providers and their non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive, PROTECTED and SECRET cloud services undergo an IRAP assessment, using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the IRAP assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

controls.title: Control: ism-1972
controls.description: Outsourced cloud service providers and their TOP SECRET cloud services, including sensitive compartmented information cloud services, undergo a security control assessment by ASD assessors (or their delegates), using the latest release of the ISM available prior to the beginning of the security control assessment (or a subsequent release), at least every 24 months.

controls.title: Control: ism-1395
controls.description: Service providers, including any subcontractors, provide an appropriate level of protection for any data entrusted to them or their services.

controls.title: Control: ism-0072
controls.description: Security requirements associated with the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data are documented in contractual arrangements with service providers and regularly reviewed to ensure they remain fit for purpose.

controls.title: Control: ism-1571
controls.description: The right to verify compliance with security requirements is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1738
controls.description: The right to verify compliance with security requirements documented in contractual arrangements with service providers is regularly exercised.

controls.title: Control: ism-1804
controls.description: Break clauses associated with failure to meet security requirements are documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-0141
controls.description: The requirement for service providers to report cyber security incidents to a designated point of contact as soon as possible after they occur or are discovered is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1794
controls.description: A minimum notification period of one month by service providers for significant changes to their own service provider arrangements is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1451
controls.description: Types of data and its ownership is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1572
controls.description: The regions or availability zones where data will be processed, stored and communicated, as well as a minimum notification period for any configuration changes, is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1573
controls.description: Access to all logs relating to an organisation’s data and services is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1574
controls.description: The storage of data in a portable manner that enables backups, service migration and service decommissioning without any loss of data is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1575
controls.description: A minimum notification period of one month for the cessation of any services by a service provider is documented in contractual arrangements with service providers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1073
controls.description: An organisation’s systems are not accessed or administered by a service provider unless a contractual arrangement exists between the organisation and the service provider to do so.

controls.title: Control: ism-2124
controls.description: Access by a service provider to an organisation’s systems is restricted to remote management tools, source network addresses and time windows explicitly approved by the organisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1576
controls.description: If an organisation’s systems are accessed or administered by a service provider in an unauthorised manner, it is treated as a cyber security incident and the organisation is immediately notified.

controls.title: Control: ism-2125
controls.description: All access to an organisation’s systems by a service provider is independently logged by the organisation in a manner that the service provider cannot modify or delete, and analysed in a timely manner to detect any anomalous, unexpected or unauthorised activity.

controls.title: Control: ism-0039
controls.description: A cyber security strategy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0047
controls.description: Organisational-level cyber security documentation is approved by the chief information security officer while system-specific cyber security documentation is approved by the system’s authorising officer.

controls.title: Control: ism-1739
controls.description: A system’s security architecture is approved prior to the development of the system.

controls.title: Control: ism-0888
controls.description: Cyber security documentation is reviewed at least annually and includes a ‘current as at \[date\]’ or equivalent statement.

controls.title: Control: ism-1602
controls.description: Cyber security documentation, including notification of subsequent changes, is communicated to all stakeholders.

controls.title: Control: ism-0041
controls.description: Systems have a system security plan that includes an overview of the system (covering the system’s purpose, the system boundary and how the system is managed) as well as an annex that covers applicable security controls from this document and any additional security controls that have been identified and implemented.

controls.title: Control: ism-0043
controls.description:
Systems have a cyber security incident response plan that covers the following:

- guidelines on what constitutes a cyber security incident
- the types of cyber security incidents likely to be encountered and the expected response to each type
- how to report cyber security incidents, internally to an organisation and externally to relevant authorities
- other parties that need to be informed in the event of a cyber security incident
- the authority, or authorities, responsible for investigating and responding to cyber security incidents
- the criteria by which an investigation of a cyber security incident would be requested from a law enforcement agency, the Australian Signals Directorate or other relevant authority
- the steps necessary to ensure the integrity of evidence relating to a cyber security incident
- system contingency measures or a reference to such details if they are in a separate document.

controls.title: Control: ism-0912
controls.description:
Systems have a change and configuration management plan that includes:

- the establishment and maintenance of authorised baseline configurations for systems
- what constitutes routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- how changes to the configuration of systems will be requested, tracked and documented
- who needs to be consulted prior to routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- who needs to approve routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- who needs to be notified of routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems
- what additional change management and configuration management processes and procedures need to be followed before, during and after routine and urgent changes to the configuration of systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-1163
controls.description:
Systems have a continuous monitoring plan that includes:

- conducting security assessment activities to identify vulnerabilities
- analysing identified vulnerabilities to determine their potential impact
- implementing mitigations based on risk, effectiveness and cost.

controls.title: Control: ism-1563
controls.description:
At the conclusion of a security control assessment for a system, a security assessment report is produced by the assessor and covers:

- the scope of the security control assessment
- the system’s strengths and weaknesses
- security risks associated with the operation of the system
- the effectiveness of the implementation of security controls
- any recommended remediation actions.

controls.title: Control: ism-1564
controls.description: At the conclusion of a security control assessment for a system, a plan of action and milestones is produced by the system owner.

controls.title: Control: ism-1973
controls.description: Non-classified systems are secured in suitably secure facilities.

controls.title: Control: ism-0810
controls.description: Classified systems are secured in facilities that meet the requirements for a security zone suitable for their classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-1974
controls.description: Non-classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in suitably secure server rooms or communications rooms.

controls.title: Control: ism-1053
controls.description: Classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in server rooms or communications rooms that meet the requirements for a security zone suitable for their classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-1975
controls.description: Non-classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in suitably secure security containers.

controls.title: Control: ism-1530
controls.description: Classified servers, network devices and cryptographic equipment are secured in security containers suitable for their classification taking into account the combination of security zones they reside in.

controls.title: Control: ism-0813
controls.description: Server rooms, communications rooms and security containers are not left in unsecured states.

controls.title: Control: ism-1074
controls.description: Keys or equivalent access mechanisms to server rooms, communications rooms and security containers are appropriately controlled.

controls.title: Control: ism-1296
controls.description: Physical security is implemented to protect network devices in public areas from physical damage or unauthorised access.

controls.title: Control: ism-1543
controls.description: An authorised RF and IR device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-0225
controls.description: Unauthorised RF and IR devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-0829
controls.description: Security measures are used to detect and respond to unauthorised RF devices in SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-2069
controls.description: An authorised photographic and video recording device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-2070
controls.description: Unauthorised photographic and video recording devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-2007
controls.description: An authorised medical device register for SECRET and TOP SECRET areas is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-2008
controls.description:
Medical devices authorised to be brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas meet, at a minimum, the following criteria:

- are listed on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods
- have been prescribed by a legally qualified medical practitioner
- have been commercially purchased within Australia
- do not have inbuilt cellular connectivity
- can operate independently of mobile devices
- where possible, have Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and other forms of wireless connectivity disabled when operating within SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-2009
controls.description: Unauthorised medical devices are not brought into SECRET and TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-0164
controls.description: Unauthorised people are prevented from observing systems, in particular workstation displays and keyboards, within facilities.

controls.title: Control: ism-0161
controls.description: IT equipment and media are secured when not in use.

controls.title: Control: ism-0252
controls.description:
Cyber security awareness training is undertaken annually by all personnel and covers:

- the purpose of the cyber security awareness training
- security appointments and contacts
- authorised use of systems and their resources
- protection of systems and their resources
- reporting of cyber security incidents and suspected compromises of systems and their resources.

controls.title: Control: ism-1565
controls.description: Tailored privileged user training is undertaken annually by all personnel with privileged access to systems and their resources.

controls.title: Control: ism-2022
controls.description: A cyber security awareness training register is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-2074
controls.description: A general-purpose AI usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0258
controls.description: A web usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1740
controls.description: Personnel dealing with banking details and payment requests are advised of what business email compromise is and how to manage and report it.

controls.title: Control: ism-2071
controls.description: Personnel dealing with user account details are advised of what social engineering attacks are, how to manage such situations and how to report them.

controls.title: Control: ism-2126
controls.description: Personnel positively identify requestors using a pre-established authentication method or independent trusted communication channel before actioning requests to modify user account details, modify banking details or conduct financial transactions.

controls.title: Control: ism-0817
controls.description: Personnel are advised of what suspicious contact via online services is and how to report it.

controls.title: Control: ism-0820
controls.description: Personnel are advised not to post work-related information on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

controls.title: Control: ism-2104
controls.description: Personnel are advised not to post information about their security clearance and briefings on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

controls.title: Control: ism-2105
controls.description: Personnel are advised to limit posting information about their work-related duties on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

controls.title: Control: ism-2106
controls.description: Personnel are advised to limit posting information about their work-related skills and experience on unauthorised online services, and to report cases where such information is posted.

controls.title: Control: ism-0821
controls.description: Personnel are advised of security risks associated with posting personal information on online services.

controls.title: Control: ism-1146
controls.description: Personnel are advised to maintain separate personal user accounts from any work user accounts they use for online services.

controls.title: Control: ism-2107
controls.description: Personnel are encouraged to use any available privacy settings to restrict who can view personal information they post on online services.

controls.title: Control: ism-0824
controls.description: Personnel are advised not to send or receive files via unauthorised online services.

controls.title: Control: ism-0181
controls.description: Cabling infrastructure is installed in accordance with relevant Australian Standards, as directed by the Australian Communications and Media Authority.

controls.title: Control: ism-1111
controls.description: Fibre-optic cables are used for cabling infrastructure instead of copper cables.

controls.title: Control: ism-0211
controls.description: A cable register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-0208
controls.description:
A cable register contains the following for each cable:

- cable identifier
- cable colour
- sensitivity/classification
- source
- destination
- location
- seal numbers (if applicable).

controls.title: Control: ism-1645
controls.description: Floor plan diagrams are developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-1646
controls.description:
Floor plan diagrams contain the following:

- cable paths (including ingress and egress points between floors)
- cable reticulation system and conduit paths
- floor concentration boxes
- wall outlet boxes
- network cabinets.

controls.title: Control: ism-0206
controls.description: Cable labelling processes, and supporting cable labelling procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1096
controls.description: Cables are labelled at each end with sufficient source and destination details to enable the physical identification and inspection of the cable.

controls.title: Control: ism-1639
controls.description: Building management cables are labelled with their purpose in black writing on a yellow background, with a minimum size of 2.5 cm x 1 cm, and attached at five-metre intervals.

controls.title: Control: ism-1640
controls.description: Cables for foreign systems installed in Australian facilities are labelled at inspection points.

controls.title: Control: ism-1820
controls.description: Cables for individual systems use a consistent colour.

controls.title: Control: ism-0926
controls.description: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED cables are coloured neither salmon pink nor red.

controls.title: Control: ism-1718
controls.description: SECRET cables are coloured salmon pink.

controls.title: Control: ism-1719
controls.description: TOP SECRET cables are coloured red.

controls.title: Control: ism-1216
controls.description: SECRET and TOP SECRET cables with non-conformant cable colouring are banded with the appropriate colour and labelled at inspection points.

controls.title: Control: ism-1112
controls.description: Cables in non-TOP SECRET areas are inspectable every five metres or less.

controls.title: Control: ism-1119
controls.description: Cables in TOP SECRET areas are fully inspectable for their entire length.

controls.title: Control: ism-0187
controls.description: SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.

controls.title: Control: ism-1821
controls.description: TOP SECRET cables, when bundled together or run in conduit, are run exclusively in their own individual cable bundle or conduit.

controls.title: Control: ism-1114
controls.description: Cable bundles or conduits sharing a common cable reticulation system have a dividing partition or visible gap between each cable bundle and conduit.

controls.title: Control: ism-1130
controls.description: In shared facilities, cables are run in an enclosed cable reticulation system.

controls.title: Control: ism-1164
controls.description: In shared facilities, conduits or the front covers of ducts, cable trays in floors and ceilings, and associated fittings are clear plastic.

controls.title: Control: ism-0195
controls.description: In shared facilities, uniquely identifiable SCEC-approved tamper-evident seals are used to seal all removable covers on TOP SECRET cable reticulation systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-0194
controls.description: In shared facilities, a visible smear of conduit glue is used to seal all plastic conduit joints and TOP SECRET conduits connected by threaded lock nuts.

controls.title: Control: ism-0201
controls.description: Labels for TOP SECRET conduits are a minimum size of 2.5 cm x 1 cm, attached at five-metre intervals and marked as ‘TS RUN’.

controls.title: Control: ism-1115
controls.description: Cables from cable trays to wall outlet boxes are run in flexible or plastic conduit.

controls.title: Control: ism-1133
controls.description: In shared facilities, TOP SECRET cables are not run in party walls.

controls.title: Control: ism-1122
controls.description: Where wall penetrations exit a TOP SECRET area into a lower classified area, TOP SECRET cables are encased in conduit with all gaps between the TOP SECRET conduit and the wall filled with an appropriate sealing compound.

controls.title: Control: ism-1105
controls.description: SECRET and TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes contain exclusively SECRET or TOP SECRET cables.

controls.title: Control: ism-1095
controls.description: Wall outlet boxes denote the systems, cable identifiers and wall outlet box identifier.

controls.title: Control: ism-1822
controls.description: Wall outlet boxes for individual systems use a consistent colour.

controls.title: Control: ism-1107
controls.description: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED wall outlet boxes are coloured neither salmon pink nor red.

controls.title: Control: ism-1720
controls.description: SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured salmon pink.

controls.title: Control: ism-1721
controls.description: TOP SECRET wall outlet boxes are coloured red.

controls.title: Control: ism-1109
controls.description: Wall outlet box covers are clear plastic.

controls.title: Control: ism-0218
controls.description: If TOP SECRET fibre-optic fly leads exceeding five metres in length are used to connect wall outlet boxes to IT equipment, they are run in a protective and easily inspected pathway that is clearly labelled at the IT equipment end with the wall outlet box’s identifier.

controls.title: Control: ism-1102
controls.description: Cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.

controls.title: Control: ism-1101
controls.description: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated as close as possible to the cabinet.

controls.title: Control: ism-1103
controls.description: In TOP SECRET areas, cable reticulation systems leading into cabinets not in server rooms or communications rooms are terminated at the boundary of the cabinet.

controls.title: Control: ism-1098
controls.description: SECRET cables are terminated in an individual cabinet; or for small systems, a cabinet with a division plate between any SECRET cables and non-SECRET cables.

controls.title: Control: ism-1100
controls.description: TOP SECRET cables are terminated in an individual TOP SECRET cabinet.

controls.title: Control: ism-0213
controls.description: SECRET and TOP SECRET cables are terminated on their own individual patch panels.

controls.title: Control: ism-0216
controls.description: TOP SECRET patch panels are installed in individual TOP SECRET cabinets.

controls.title: Control: ism-0217
controls.description:
Where spatial constraints demand non-TOP SECRET patch panels be installed in the same cabinet as a TOP SECRET patch panel:

- a physical barrier in the cabinet is provided to separate patch panels
- only personnel holding a Positive Vetting security clearance have access to the cabinet
- approval from the TOP SECRET system’s authorising officer is obtained prior to installation.

controls.title: Control: ism-1116
controls.description: A visible gap exists between TOP SECRET cabinets and non-TOP SECRET cabinets.

controls.title: Control: ism-0198
controls.description: When penetrating a TOP SECRET audio secure room, the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation is consulted and all directions provided are complied with.

controls.title: Control: ism-1123
controls.description: A power distribution board with a feed from an Uninterruptible Power Supply is used to power all TOP SECRET IT equipment.

controls.title: Control: ism-0250
controls.description: IT equipment meets industry and government standards relating to electromagnetic interference/electromagnetic compatibility.

controls.title: Control: ism-1884
controls.description: Emanation security doctrine produced by ASD for the management of emanation security matters is complied with.

controls.title: Control: ism-1137
controls.description: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems within fixed facilities contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.

controls.title: Control: ism-0249
controls.description: System owners deploying SECRET or TOP SECRET systems in mobile platforms, or as a deployable capability, contact ASD for an emanation security risk assessment.

controls.title: Control: ism-0246
controls.description: When an emanation security risk assessment is required, it is sought as early as possible in a system’s life cycle.

controls.title: Control: ism-1885
controls.description: Recommended actions contained within emanation security mitigation advice issued for systems are implemented by system owners.

controls.title: Control: ism-1078
controls.description: A telephone system usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0229
controls.description: Personnel are advised of the permitted sensitivity or classification of information that can be discussed over internal and external telephone systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-0230
controls.description: Personnel are advised of security risks posed by non-secure telephone systems in areas where sensitive or classified conversations can occur.

controls.title: Control: ism-0231
controls.description: When using cryptographic equipment to permit different levels of conversation for different kinds of connections, telephone systems give a visual indication of what kind of connection has been made.

controls.title: Control: ism-0232
controls.description: Telephone systems used for sensitive or classified conversations encrypt all traffic that passes over external systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-0233
controls.description: Cordless telephone handsets and headsets are not used for sensitive or classified conversations unless all communications are encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.

controls.title: Control: ism-0235
controls.description: Speakerphones are not used on telephone systems in TOP SECRET areas unless the telephone system is located in an audio secure room, the room is audio secure during conversations and only personnel involved in conversations are present in the room.

controls.title: Control: ism-0236
controls.description: Off-hook audio protection features are used on telephone systems in areas where background conversations may exceed the sensitivity or classification that the telephone system is authorised for communicating.

controls.title: Control: ism-0931
controls.description: In SECRET and TOP SECRET areas, push-to-talk handsets or push-to-talk headsets are used to meet any off-hook audio protection requirements.

controls.title: Control: ism-1562
controls.description: Video conferencing and IP telephony infrastructure is hardened.

controls.title: Control: ism-0546
controls.description: When video conferencing or IP telephony traffic passes through a gateway containing a firewall or proxy, a video-aware or voice-aware firewall or proxy is used.

controls.title: Control: ism-0548
controls.description: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are established using a secure session initiation protocol.

controls.title: Control: ism-0547
controls.description: Video conferencing and IP telephony calls are conducted using a secure real-time transport protocol.

controls.title: Control: ism-0554
controls.description: An encrypted and non-replayable two-way authentication scheme is used for call authentication and authorisation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0553
controls.description: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on a video conferencing network, including call setup and changing settings.

controls.title: Control: ism-0555
controls.description: Authentication and authorisation is used for all actions on an IP telephony network, including registering a new IP phone, changing phone users, changing settings and accessing voicemail.

controls.title: Control: ism-0551
controls.description:
IP telephony is configured such that:

- IP phones authenticate themselves to the call controller upon registration
- auto-registration is disabled and only authorised devices are allowed to access the network
- unauthorised devices are blocked by default
- all unused and prohibited functionality is disabled.

controls.title: Control: ism-1014
controls.description: Individual logins are implemented for IP phones used for SECRET or TOP SECRET conversations.

controls.title: Control: ism-0549
controls.description: Video conferencing and IP telephony traffic is physically or logically separated from other data traffic.

controls.title: Control: ism-0556
controls.description: Workstations are not connected to video conferencing units or IP phones unless the workstation or the device uses virtual local area networks or similar mechanisms to maintain separation between video conferencing, IP telephony and other data traffic.

controls.title: Control: ism-0558
controls.description: IP phones used in public areas do not have the ability to access data networks, voicemail and directory services.

controls.title: Control: ism-0559
controls.description: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-SECRET workstations in SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-1450
controls.description: Microphones (including headsets and USB handsets) and webcams are not used with non-TOP SECRET workstations in TOP SECRET areas.

controls.title: Control: ism-1019
controls.description: A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1805
controls.description:
A denial of service response plan for video conferencing and IP telephony services contains the following:

- how to identify signs of a denial-of-service attack
- how to identify the source of a denial-of-service attack
- how capabilities can be maintained during a denial-of-service attack
- what actions can be taken to respond to a denial-of-service attack.

controls.title: Control: ism-0588
controls.description: An MFD usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0245
controls.description: MFDs are not connected to digital telephone systems.

controls.title: Control: ism-1854
controls.description: Human users authenticate to MFDs before they can print, scan or copy documents.

controls.title: Control: ism-0590
controls.description: Authentication measures for MFDs are the same strength as those used for workstations on networks they are connected to.

controls.title: Control: ism-0589
controls.description: MFDs are not used to scan or copy documents above the sensitivity or classification of networks they are connected to.

controls.title: Control: ism-1855
controls.description: Use of MFDs for printing, scanning and copying purposes, including the capture of shadow copies of documents, are centrally logged.

controls.title: Control: ism-1036
controls.description: MFDs are placed in areas where their use can be observed.

controls.title: Control: ism-2075
controls.description: Fax machines, and online fax services, are not used for sending or receiving fax messages.

controls.title: Control: ism-1297
controls.description: Legal advice is sought prior to allowing privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers to access systems or data.

controls.title: Control: ism-1400
controls.description: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.

controls.title: Control: ism-1866
controls.description: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are prevented from storing classified data on their privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers.

controls.title: Control: ism-2095
controls.description: Personnel using privately owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data are disallowed from granting access to unapproved artificial intelligence agents.

controls.title: Control: ism-0694
controls.description: Privately owned mobile devices and desktop computers do not access SECRET and TOP SECRET systems or data.

controls.title: Control: ism-1482
controls.description: Personnel using organisation-owned mobile devices or desktop computers to access classified systems or data have enforced separation of classified data and personal data.

controls.title: Control: ism-0874
controls.description: Mobile devices and desktop computers access the internet via an organisation’s internet gateway rather than via a direct connection to the internet.

controls.title: Control: ism-0705
controls.description: When accessing an organisation’s network via a VPN connection, split tunnelling is disabled.

controls.title: Control: ism-1533
controls.description: A mobile device management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1195
controls.description: Mobile Device Management solutions that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Management, version 4.0 or later, are used to enforce mobile device management policy.

controls.title: Control: ism-1867
controls.description: Mobile devices that access OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED systems or data use mobile platforms that have completed a Common Criteria evaluation against the Protection Profile for Mobile Device Fundamentals, version 3.3 or later, and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated ASD security configuration guide.

controls.title: Control: ism-0687
controls.description: Mobile devices that access SECRET or TOP SECRET systems or data use mobile platforms that have been issued an Approval for Use by ASD and are operated in accordance with the latest version of their associated Australian Communications Security Instruction.

controls.title: Control: ism-0869
controls.description: Mobile devices encrypt their internal storage and any removable media using ASD-approved cryptography.

controls.title: Control: ism-1868
controls.description: SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices do not use removable media unless approved beforehand by ASD.

controls.title: Control: ism-1085
controls.description: Mobile devices encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.

controls.title: Control: ism-2108
controls.description: Mobile applications encrypt all sensitive or classified data communicated over public network infrastructure using ASD-approved cryptography.

controls.title: Control: ism-1886
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured to operate in a supervised (or equivalent) mode.

controls.title: Control: ism-2096
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured to enforce separation between organisational and personal mobile applications and data.

controls.title: Control: ism-2097
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured with always on VPN functionality.

controls.title: Control: ism-1887
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured with remote locate and wipe functionality.

controls.title: Control: ism-1888
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured with secure password-based lock screens.

controls.title: Control: ism-2098
controls.description: Mobile devices are configured to prevent data transfers over Universal Serial Bus connections.

controls.title: Control: ism-0863
controls.description: Mobile devices prevent personnel from installing non-approved applications once provisioned.

controls.title: Control: ism-0864
controls.description: Mobile devices prevent personnel from disabling or modifying security functionality once provisioned.

controls.title: Control: ism-1366
controls.description: Security updates are applied to mobile devices as soon as they become available.

controls.title: Control: ism-1082
controls.description: A mobile device usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1083
controls.description: Personnel are advised of the sensitivity or classification permitted for voice and data communications when using mobile devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1299
controls.description:
Personnel are advised to take the following precautions when using mobile devices:

- never leave mobile devices or removable media unattended, including by placing them in checked-in luggage or leaving them in hotel safes
- never store credentials with mobile devices that they grant access to, such as in laptop computer bags
- never lend mobile devices or removable media to untrusted people, even if briefly
- never allow untrusted people to connect their mobile devices or removable media to your mobile devices, including for charging
- never connect mobile devices to designated charging stations or wall outlet charging ports
- never use gifted or unauthorised peripherals, chargers or removable media with mobile devices
- never use removable media for data transfers or backups that have not been checked for malicious code beforehand
- avoid reuse of removable media once used with other parties’ systems or mobile devices
- avoid connecting mobile devices to open or untrusted Wi-Fi networks
- consider disabling any communications capabilities of mobile devices when not in use, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Near Field Communication and ultra-wideband
- consider periodically rebooting mobile devices
- consider using a VPN connection to encrypt all cellular and wireless communications
- consider using encrypted email or messaging apps for all communications.

controls.title: Control: ism-0240
controls.description: Paging, Multimedia Message Service, Short Message Service and messaging apps are not used to communicate sensitive or classified data.

controls.title: Control: ism-1196
controls.description: Non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are configured to remain undiscoverable to other Bluetooth devices except during Bluetooth pairing.

controls.title: Control: ism-1200
controls.description: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed using Secure Connections, preferably with Numeric Comparison if supported.

controls.title: Control: ism-1198
controls.description: Bluetooth pairing for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices is performed in a manner such that connections are only made between intended Bluetooth devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1199
controls.description: Bluetooth pairings for non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED mobile devices are removed when there is no longer a requirement for their use.

controls.title: Control: ism-0682
controls.description: Bluetooth functionality is not enabled on SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-2099
controls.description: Mobile devices are not connected to the infotainment systems of connected vehicles.

controls.title: Control: ism-2100
controls.description: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices within or near connected vehicles.

controls.title: Control: ism-2101
controls.description: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted within or near connected vehicles.

controls.title: Control: ism-0866
controls.description: Sensitive or classified data is not viewed on mobile devices in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of the screen of a mobile device being observed.

controls.title: Control: ism-1145
controls.description: Privacy filters are applied to the screens of SECRET and TOP SECRET mobile devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1644
controls.description: Sensitive or classified phone calls and conversations are not conducted in public locations unless care is taken to reduce the chance of conversations being overheard.

controls.title: Control: ism-0871
controls.description: Mobile devices are kept under continual direct supervision when being actively used.

controls.title: Control: ism-0870
controls.description: Mobile devices are carried or stored in a secured state when not being actively used.

controls.title: Control: ism-1084
controls.description: If unable to carry or store mobile devices in a secured state, they are physically transferred in a security briefcase or an approved multi-use satchel, pouch or transit bag.

controls.title: Control: ism-0701
controls.description: Mobile device emergency sanitisation processes, and supporting mobile device emergency sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0702
controls.description: If a cryptographic zeroise or sanitise function is provided for cryptographic keys on a SECRET or TOP SECRET mobile device, the function is used as part of mobile device emergency sanitisation processes and procedures.

controls.title: Control: ism-1298
controls.description: Personnel are advised of privacy and security risks when travelling overseas with mobile devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1554
controls.description:
If travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel are:

- issued with newly provisioned user accounts, mobile devices and removable media from a pool of dedicated travel devices which are used solely for work-related activities
- advised on how to apply and inspect tamper seals to key areas of mobile devices
- advised to avoid taking any personal mobile devices, especially if rooted or jailbroken.

controls.title: Control: ism-1555
controls.description:
Before travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- record all details of the mobile devices being taken, such as product types, serial numbers and International Mobile Equipment Identity numbers
- update all operating systems and applications
- remove all non-essential data, applications and user accounts
- backup all remaining data, applications and settings.

controls.title: Control: ism-1088
controls.description:
Personnel report the potential compromise of mobile devices, removable media or credentials to their organisation as soon as possible, especially if they:

- provide credentials to foreign government officials
- decrypt mobile devices for foreign government officials
- have mobile devices taken out of sight by foreign government officials
- have mobile devices or removable media stolen, including if later returned
- lose mobile devices or removable media, including if later found
- observe unusual behaviour of mobile devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1300
controls.description:
Upon returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices, personnel take the following actions:

- sanitise and reset mobile devices, including all removable media
- decommission any credentials that left their possession during their travel
- report if significant doubt exists as to the integrity of any mobile devices or removable media.

controls.title: Control: ism-1556
controls.description:
If returning from travelling overseas with mobile devices to high or extreme risk countries, personnel take the following additional actions:

- reset credentials used with mobile devices, including those used for remote access to their organisation’s systems
- monitor user accounts for any indicators of compromise, such as failed logon attempts.

controls.title: Control: ism-0280
controls.description: If procuring an evaluated product, a product that has completed a PP-based evaluation, including against all applicable PP modules (as well as a software bill of materials assessment if applicable), is selected in preference to one that has completed an EAL-based evaluation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0285
controls.description: Evaluated products are delivered in a manner consistent with any delivery procedures defined in associated evaluation documentation.

controls.title: Control: ism-0286
controls.description: When procuring high assurance information technology (IT) equipment, ASD is contacted for any equipment-specific delivery procedures.

controls.title: Control: ism-0289
controls.description: Evaluated products are installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with vendor guidance.

controls.title: Control: ism-0290
controls.description: High assurance IT equipment is installed, configured, administered and operated in an evaluated configuration and in accordance with ASD guidance.

controls.title: Control: ism-1551
controls.description: An IT equipment management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1913
controls.description: Approved configurations for IT equipment are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1858
controls.description: IT equipment is hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur.

controls.title: Control: ism-0336
controls.description: A networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-1869
controls.description: A non-networked IT equipment register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-0294
controls.description: IT equipment, except for high assurance IT equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-0296
controls.description: ASD’s approval is sought before applying labels to external surfaces of high assurance IT equipment.

controls.title: Control: ism-0293
controls.description: IT equipment is classified based on the highest sensitivity or classification of data that it is approved for processing, storing or communicating.

controls.title: Control: ism-1599
controls.description: IT equipment is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-1079
controls.description: ASD’s approval is sought before undertaking any maintenance or repairs to high assurance IT equipment.

controls.title: Control: ism-0305
controls.description: Maintenance or repairs of IT equipment are carried out on site by an appropriately cleared technician.

controls.title: Control: ism-0307
controls.description: If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the IT equipment and associated media are sanitised before maintenance or repairs.

controls.title: Control: ism-0306
controls.description:
If an appropriately cleared technician is not used to undertake maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, the technician is escorted by someone who:

- has the authority to direct the technician
- is appropriately cleared and briefed
- is sufficiently familiar with the IT equipment to understand the work being undertaken
- takes all responsible measures to ensure the integrity of the IT equipment
- takes due care to ensure that data is not disclosed.

controls.title: Control: ism-0310
controls.description: IT equipment maintained or repaired off site is handled at facilities approved for handling the sensitivity or classification of the IT equipment.

controls.title: Control: ism-1598
controls.description: Following maintenance or repairs to IT equipment, it is inspected to confirm that it retains its approved configuration and that no unauthorised modifications have been made.

controls.title: Control: ism-0313
controls.description: IT equipment sanitisation processes, and supporting IT equipment sanitisation procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1741
controls.description: IT equipment destruction processes, and supporting IT equipment destruction procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-0311
controls.description: IT equipment containing media is sanitised by removing the media from the IT equipment or by sanitising the media in situ.

controls.title: Control: ism-1742
controls.description: IT equipment that cannot be sanitised is destroyed.

controls.title: Control: ism-1218
controls.description: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data, is sanitised in situ.

controls.title: Control: ism-0312
controls.description: IT equipment, including associated media, that is located overseas and has processed, stored or communicated AUSTEO or AGAO data that cannot be sanitised in situ, is returned to Australia for destruction.

controls.title: Control: ism-0315
controls.description: High assurance IT equipment is destroyed prior to its disposal.

controls.title: Control: ism-0317
controls.description: At least three pages of random text with no blank areas are printed on each colour printer cartridge or MFD print drum.

controls.title: Control: ism-1219
controls.description: MFD print drums and image transfer rollers are inspected and destroyed if there is remnant toner that cannot be removed or a print is visible on the image transfer roller.

controls.title: Control: ism-1220
controls.description: Printer and MFD platens are inspected and destroyed if any text or images are retained on the platen.

controls.title: Control: ism-1221
controls.description: Printers and MFDs are checked to ensure no pages are trapped in the paper path due to a paper jam.

controls.title: Control: ism-0318
controls.description: When unable to sanitise printer cartridges or MFD print drums, they are destroyed as per electrostatic memory devices.

controls.title: Control: ism-1534
controls.description: Printer ribbons in printers and MFDs are removed and destroyed.

controls.title: Control: ism-1076
controls.description: Televisions and computer monitors with minor burn-in or image persistence are sanitised by displaying a solid white image on the screen for an extended period.

controls.title: Control: ism-1222
controls.description: Televisions and computer monitors that cannot be sanitised are destroyed.

controls.title: Control: ism-1223
controls.description:
Memory in network devices is sanitised using the following processes, in order of preference:

- following device-specific guidance provided in evaluation documentation
- following vendor sanitisation guidance
- loading a dummy configuration file, performing a factory reset and then reinstalling firmware.

controls.title: Control: ism-1550
controls.description: IT equipment disposal processes, and supporting IT equipment disposal procedures, are developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1217
controls.description: Labels and markings indicating the owner, sensitivity, classification or any other marking that can associate IT equipment with its prior use are removed prior to its disposal.

controls.title: Control: ism-0321
controls.description: When disposing of IT equipment that has been designed or modified to meet emanation security standards, ASD is contacted for requirements relating to its disposal.

controls.title: Control: ism-0316
controls.description: Following sanitisation, destruction or declassification, a formal administrative decision is made to release IT equipment, or its waste, into the public domain.

controls.title: Control: ism-1549
controls.description: A media management policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1359
controls.description: A removable media usage policy is developed, implemented and maintained.

controls.title: Control: ism-1713
controls.description: A removable media register is developed, implemented, maintained and regularly verified.

controls.title: Control: ism-0332
controls.description: Media, except for internally mounted fixed media within information technology equipment, is labelled with protective markings reflecting its sensitivity or classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-0323
controls.description: Media is classified to the highest sensitivity or classification of data it stores, unless the media has been classified to a higher sensitivity or classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-0337
controls.description: Media is only used with systems that are authorised to process, store or communicate its sensitivity or classification.

controls.title: Control: ism-0325
controls.description: Any media connected to a system with a higher sensitivity or classification than the media is reclassified to the higher sensitivity or classification, unless the media is read-only or the system has a mechanism through which read-only access can be ensured.

controls.title: Control: ism-0330
controls.description: Before reclassifying media to a lower sensitivity or classification, the media is sanitised or destroyed, and a formal administrative decision is made to reclassify it.

controls.title: Control: ism-1059
controls.description: All data stored on media is encrypted using ASD-approved cryptography.

controls.title: Control: ism-0459
controls.description: Full disk encryption, or partial encryption where access controls only allow writing to encrypted partitions or volumes, is implemented when encrypting media.

controls.title: Control: ism-2109
controls.description: Pre-boot authentication using passwords, or managed network-based key release, is implemented for media containing encrypted system volumes.

controls.title: Control: ism-0831
controls.description: Media is handled in a manner suitable for its sensitivity or classification.
